PROJECT 02 / COMPUTER VISION & DESKTOP SYSTEMS

Computer Vision Desktop Automation

Turning uncertain pixels into verified actions.

A Windows application that uses computer vision and OCR to coordinate actions across up to four application windows, with explicit state checks and independent recovery.

  • Python
  • OpenCV
  • Tesseract OCR
  • PySide6

OverviewArchitectureEngineering decisionsTesting & evidenceLessons & next steps

Built to solve a practical problem.
Documented with the tradeoffs.

01 / THE PROJECT

Make the uncertain observable.

This application was developed for Fish! An Anime RNG on Roblox. It watches for the Hallows’ Eve event, selects eligible characters, reads mutation labels, and puts characters away when the event ends. The engineering problem is coordinating those actions when visual evidence is incomplete and input can arrive late.

The problem

A desktop interface is not a stable API. Windows overlap, inventory layouts change, animations hide controls, and an accepted key press may not change the game immediately. Coordinating several windows requires the application to keep track of what it intended, what it sent, and what the screen actually confirms.

What’s implemented

Visual event and inventory detection
Use OpenCV matching and image processing to locate relevant regions, with Tesseract OCR for text and mutation labels.
Action state for each window
Track targets, pending inputs, retries, and visual confirmation separately for up to four windows.
Prioritized cleanup and recovery
Handle the end of an event before less urgent work, reject stale scan results, and let healthy windows continue when another window needs recovery.
Bounded background work
Keep slower scans off the foreground input worker and limit outstanding jobs and UI messages.
Diagnostics and maintenance
Expose timestamped logs, capture previews, and independent deadlines for preventing idle timeouts in a native Qt interface.

02 / HOW IT FITS TOGETHER

Clear responsibilities.

Technology choices

Python + OpenCV + NumPy
Process small capture regions and identify visual structure in inventory and event banners.
Tesseract OCR
Read text that visual matching alone cannot classify, while keeping slower recognition off urgent paths.
PySide6
Present window status, controls, settings, and diagnostics in a native Qt application.
Windows APIs + background threads
Verify foreground ownership, serialize input, and observe events without blocking the action worker.

03 / ENGINEERING DECISIONS

The interesting parts.

01

A sent key is not a completed action.

Repeating a toggle too quickly can undo an input that arrived late. The application records the intended slot and accepted input, then uses two fresh matching observations to confirm equipment state. A hidden inventory remains uncertain; it does not become success merely because a key was sent. Retry guards and retries that only release keys protect against duplicate toggles.

The tradeoff

Waiting for reliable evidence adds latency. Conservative checks can require another capture or rescan, but preserve the distinction between an attempted action and an observed result.

02

Keep slow recognition away from urgent work.

Mutation OCR runs on copied captures in a bounded executor. Results for each event are checked against the current state before they can authorize an action. The foreground worker can service another ready window while a scan finishes, and cleanup at the end of an event interrupts less urgent work. Deadlines for preventing idle timeouts are scheduled independently so unresolved maintenance cannot suppress them indefinitely.

The tradeoff

Only one worker controls foreground input, so actions remain serialized. This avoids competing focus changes, while bounded queues favor current state over an unlimited backlog.

04 / TESTING & EVIDENCE

What the evidence supports.

The repository’s recorded version 3.5.1 validation log reports 12 of 12 regression suites passing. Coverage includes delayed and dropped inputs, stale OCR, hidden inventories, disconnected clients, event interruptions, and Qt interface behavior. Image processing and offscreen Qt checks use real code; Windows input and timing scenarios are simulated. These are recorded repository results, not a new live test performed for this portfolio.

05 / REFLECTION

Lessons and what comes next.

Reliable automation needs uncertainty to be an explicit state. Separating observation, input, and confirmation makes failures easier to diagnose, while bounded work and independent recovery keep one difficult window from consuming the entire session.

Current limitations

The implementation targets a specific game interface and requires visible content. Tracked windows must share event timing, and input takes foreground focus. Visual confirmation cannot prove server acceptance. Simulated tests do not establish overnight reliability or guarantee that input intended to prevent idle timeouts prevents server disconnects.

Next engineering steps

  • Expand validation on real Windows setups and display scales.
  • Collect reproducible captures for new interface failures.
  • Continue separating tightly coupled scheduling and recognition code.
